Domains closed to meals/workouts/goals with Domain.legacyKey. Current regular/directory routes unchanged; links/FIFO/other defaults property-list types remain rejected and open follow-ons.

authority.capture: Introduce immutable failed-origin observation, separate from Loaded boundary and availability flags. Under LocalStore write serialization and filesystem transaction serialization, lstat existing root identity, lstat selected path ENOENT, fetch only the fixed standard-defaults key, retain typed exact value. Data must fail the same plain JSONDecoder/JSONFieldAudit/HealthRecordValidation used for legacy loading. Any String is unavailable under the existing Data-only migration. Healthy Data, empty valid arrays, absent keys and missing/replaced/linked roots confer no permission.
authority.review: Capture at recovery review entry before presenting selectable replacements; retain typed observations per domain in view-owned review state. Pass the selected subset into Payload before explicit confirmation. Retry uses the same observations and rejects changes; Back closes them with the review. Fresh selection captures independently. Never recapture a changed origin silently at prepare/commit.
authority.token: Versioned value includes domain, fixed key, root device/inode and exact tag plus raw Data bytes or original String UTF-16 code units. Equality uses exact canonical token bytes/digest, never Swift String canonical-equivalence equality or String(describing:). Avoid Foundation implementation-class identities. Token carries bounded immutable content needed for private preservation, not a stale failed-read boolean.
authority.limits: Maximum 4,194,304 raw bytes per failed Data or String UTF-16 encoding, maximum three domains and 12,582,912 total raw origin bytes. Check length before copying/encoding; reject overflow without truncation. String encoder rejects any bridge/roundtrip that changes observed UTF-16 units. UserDefaults fetching itself can allocate; do not claim a preallocation bound on Foundation object retrieval.

serialization.prepare: Verify root, path absence, fixed-key tag/exact bytes, and still-failed legacy decoding before ConversationFiles protects .previous. Thread selected origin observations through ConversationFiles and BackupFileTransaction to stage preservation; only explicitly supplied valid token permits bypass of194missing-selected-leaf rejection. Never relax link or special-file rejection. Verify again after detached preparation; any error discards the stage.
serialization.commit: LocalStore revision/owner/canCommit checks remain. Retain a typed origin validator in transaction; verify under existing BackupFileTransaction and HealthRecoveryCopies locks immediately before directory installation, after source/provider/photo and private-copy checks. Final check re-fetches actual standard defaults and checks root identity/path absence/type/exact raw and still-failed decode. All cooperating app writers use the same ordering. No cross-store atomic CAS or guarantee against an external process changing defaults after the final observation.
serialization.defaultLifetime: Never delete or rewrite legacy key on recovery success/failure/cancel. Installed valid current file takes precedence. Unexplained later removal of a current file may expose unchanged legacy failure, never new replacement permission; full reset must erase the known legacy keys as already required and explicitly verify that behavior before acceptance. No legacy intents imported/replayed.

privateProvenance.schema: Manifest version2 adds optional domain-to-origin descriptors; version1 reads unchanged. For legacy origins retain legacy-origin-<domain>.json containing explicit schemaVersion1/domain/fixedKey/type and base64 exact payload (Data bytes or UTF-16LE bytes), bounded by declared limits. Newly encoded envelope is exact captured value provenance, not the original preferences plist bytes. Fixed safe filenames; no user-supplied key/path.
privateProvenance.stage: Write provenance only inside uninstalled stage before replacements; preserve selected meals photos and device-intent provenance with existing private-copy rules, including mixed file-origin/legacy-origin recovery. No fabricated domain.json or [] for an absent current path. Manifest domains includes each actually retained origin. Keep current/prior/conversations/private copies and healthy domains under existing contracts.
privateProvenance.catalog: A well-formed retained legacy origin has DomainPreview.state unavailable, nil recordCount and a provenance digest; not notIncluded/readable. Catalog validates envelope limits/domain/key/type/digest and manifest association. Damaged/missing provenance is unavailable/incomplete, never a readable fallback. Record/photo export remains disabled for this origin; no silent legacy-to-current decode. Later transactions must carry the complete envelope unchanged; dedupe can reuse only exact equivalent provenance.

productCopy.wording: For selected legacy origins, replace file-only preservation wording with: The older saved data will stay in a private recovery copy on this device. Review confirmation, genuine error, recovery success, private catalog and general unavailable-data notice for honesty; no keys/hashes/schema jargon.
productCopy.scope: Inspect actual main/compact, light/dark and largest text for changed native surfaces, using the continuing critic. Existing screenshots do not establish new copy acceptance. Ordinary file-origin wording stays accurate.

Negative controls: absent key, valid empty/nonempty legacy Data, unsupported number/bool/array/dictionary/date, missing root, linked root, selected symlink/dangling/FIFO/directory or current healthy file; current regular/directory behavior matches declared existing contract.

Changes between review/preparation/finalcommit: still-malformed byte change, tag change, canonical-equivalent but distinct String code units, key removal, now-readable Data, new current file/root replacement. Each must reject without installing replacement; record any prior-retirement/stage metadata side effects honestly.

Cancellation before capture/during preservation/before install, write failure, changed selected provider/record/photo/source, revision/owner/intent changes. Retained origin and existing no-stale-commit/cancel/cleanup contracts remain.
